doc.title: Christian McBride interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996

title: Tonight's set and talking to the audience
summary: McBride talks about the set, Joey Calderazzo's debut with the band, and why communicating with the audience matters.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: You can tell your musical influences just from the set you picked to play. You didn’t have much time but you put in quite a group of things there.
Well thank you. It was rough, I was getting nervous for a minute.

Seeing the audience and I kept looking at the clock you know, my head was going back and forth, and tonight marks the debut of Joey Calderazzo as a member of the band so I was listening to Joey, watching the audience and watching the clock at the same time. So it was rough.
Well your James Brown step came off. You know I think it’s a — I like the way you talk to the audience and I think it’s something that a lot of musicians don’t have. It’s important.

Well you know I’ve always believed that presentation is just as important as the music sounding good, I mean because I mean people like it when you try to communicate to them and try to explain a little of what’s going on and you know they like that so that draws them in to the music even more. I mean the music has to be good first and foremost. I mean if the music is not happening it doesn’t mean anything. But when the music is sounding good and you verbally try to communicate to the audience, they really appreciate that.
